items.action: Upgrade self-managed GitLab to 19.2.8, 19.3.4 or 19.4.2 immediately — an internet-exposed instance holds source code, pipeline secrets, deploy keys and runner tokens.
items.details: Affected: 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.4, 19.4 before 19.4.2. Researcher 'joaxcar' reported it via GitLab's HackerOne program; the same release fixes 5 High, 14 Medium and 4 Low issues. GitLab.com is already patched; no exploitation in the wild reported as of Oct 12, and it's not yet on CISA's KEV.
items.summary: GitLab's October 12 patch release fixes CVE-2026-97229, an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler that lets unauthenticated attackers run arbitrary code on self-managed CE/EE servers via a crafted regex in pipeline configuration.
items.title: GitLab patches CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE in CI/CD regex compiler

items.action: Patch SMA 1000 to 12.4.3-03670 or 12.5.0-03082 now and hunt exposed appliances for abnormal traffic and signs of lateral movement.
items.details: The flaw lets remote attackers direct the appliance to issue requests on their behalf and reach internal functionality. Patches: 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082 (platform-hotfix). First signs of exploitation were detected Oct 8 by Defused Cyber and Previdian; SonicWall has not yet updated its advisory to reflect it. In June, the same product was hit by zero-days (CVE-2026-15409/15410) used to deploy Java web shells and the KNUCKLEBALL malware.
items.summary: CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10.0), a pre-authenticated server-side request forgery in SonicWall Secure Mobile Access 1000, is being actively exploited within days of the October 6 patch: Previdian observed 135 attempts from two US-based IPs.
items.title: Critical SonicWall SMA 1000 SSRF under active exploitation — 135 attempts and counting

items.action: Upgrade to 2026.7.0 (or the latest patched minor on your branch). If patching is delayed, disable PDF uploads or limit upload rights to trusted users.
items.details: CVE-2026-55674 fixed in 2026.7.0 / 2026.6.1 / 2026.5.2 / 2026.1.6; CVE-2026-55420 fixed in 2026.6.0 / 2026.5.1 / 2026.4.2 / 2026.1.5. Both were reported to Discourse in June; no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation. Discourse powers 22,000+ communities, many running open-registration forums.
items.summary: Research published Oct 7 by SL Cyber details two Discourse flaws: CVE-2026-55674 (cache poisoning that serves attacker JavaScript to anonymous visitors) and CVE-2026-55420 (an image-upload race leading to arbitrary file read/write via ImageMagick and GhostScript).
items.title: Discourse patches JS-injection cache poisoning and image-upload file theft

items.details: State filings confirm 298,647 affected in Texas and 69,526 in South Carolina (one aggregation cites ~8.2M nationwide; iRhythm has not disclosed a total). Stolen: names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, dates of birth, account and device serial numbers, insurance numbers. The threat actor contacted the company June 9 demanding payment to prevent publication. Medical devices, clinical systems and patient safety were unaffected.
items.summary: iRhythm Technologies is notifying hundreds of thousands of patients after hackers gained access to third-party-hosted business applications through social engineering and exfiltrated data between June 3 and 8, 2026.
items.title: iRhythm breach: hackers stole data on 360,000+ cardiac patients

items.details: Malware was found on the NCG computer Oct 5, isolated Oct 6, and disclosed Oct 11. Exposed fields: names, genders, dates of birth, email addresses, telephone numbers — no passwords or payment data. Credentials were reset; investigators are still checking for data leaks online. Affected brands include Big Echo and DK Dining.
items.summary: Japanese karaoke giant Daiichi Kosho disclosed that malware on a contractor's (Nippon Columbia Group) employee PC may have exposed ~8.63 million customer and 93,000 employee records — a supply-chain breach with no confirmed exfiltration yet.
items.title: Malware at contractor exposes ~8.7M Daiichi Kosho customer records

items.details: The listing is the gang's unverified claim, with publication threatened soon. Akira remains one of the year's most prolific data-extortion crews; claims of this size typically precede staged leaks to force payment.
items.summary: The Akira ransomware group listed the Louis Fusco Group on its leak site on Oct 12, claiming theft of 465GB of corporate data including employee passport and driver's license scans, project specifications, drawings and client/partner information.
items.title: Akira claims 465GB heist from Louis Fusco Group

items.details: No data volumes or exfiltration details published yet; the listing is the group's claim and is unverified.
items.summary: The Orova ransomware crew added Amantya Technologies, an Indian technology company, to its leak site — disclosed Oct 12. Orova has listed ~47 victims since first appearing in May 2026.
items.title: Orova ransomware lists Indian tech firm Amantya Technologies

items.details: Two cases registered from January allege the accused ran call centres in Australia, Cambodia and elsewhere to defraud victims in India and abroad, routing proceeds through mule bank accounts. 55 people have been arrested so far in the two cases.
items.summary: Telangana Cyber Security Bureau teams searched homes in Sathupalli and Rajugudem (Khammam district) linked to a cybercrime probe involving over ₹1,000 crore in transactions, seizing a Mercedes-Benz car, six phones, two laptops and property documents.
items.title: Telangana CSB raids homes in ₹1,000-crore cybercrime probe

items.details: The victim transferred money via RTGS to multiple accounts under the pretext of account verification, then reported through the 1930 national cybercrime helpline. Dakshina Kannada Cyber Crime Police registered a case under IT Act 66C/66D and BNS provisions.
items.summary: A man from Puttur, Karnataka, transferred ₹1,31,50,000 between Sept 2 and Oct 6 to fraudsters impersonating Mumbai Police and ATS officers over WhatsApp video calls, who accused him of funding the Pahalgam attack and kept him under a month-long 'digital arrest'.
items.title: Puttur man loses ₹1.31 crore in 'digital arrest' scam
